title: Screen P112 tetrad coefficient fusion under relaxed rank ceilings
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

This is a scoped screen, not a construction or a κ improvement. Across the 14 selected P112 tetrads, a source-bound unimodular output change reduces all 56 update terms from copy rank 2 to rank 1. Composing that change into the selected gauge44 centre cut increases its support from 176 to 286 coefficients and exposes a dirty-baseline mismatch. If the original dirty vector `d` is separately retained, the exact correction `C = S - S_new` uses 281 coefficients, for 567 total incidences (+391 over the original cut).

A source-side identity avoids requiring a second `d` stream algebraically: `S^T(d + U K x) - J x = S^T(d + K x)`, with `J = C^T U K`. Charging each `J` coefficient as one hypothetical rank-1 unit gives a three-tetrad complex ceiling of `0.004756582174`. This clears `0.003` only as an incidence sensitivity; source access, a native schedule, scalar pricing, restoration and the complete bit-side invoice remain open. The other conditional ceilings are `0.026445058957` with a separately available dirty correction and `0.038865401047` if a producer supplies the full transformed output without a separately priced basis conversion. The inherited bit-side ceiling is `0.052325479379`. No κ above `0.003` is realized or claimed; selected κ remains `0.001672660197076918`.

## Task and overlap

Task `coverage-law-change`, priority revision 6. This is a scoped follow-up to [PR #3344](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3344), [PR #3566](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3566), and [PR #3567](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3567). The cached overlap scan covered 394 open PRs and 2,319 discussions, but its refresh failed; it is not a novelty certificate. The two package bases are `ebd6b92c43239d76b1a59e29f574563494388f6a` and `b1ef0a5585418590320806c967383584c645132b`.

## Validation

Replayed with CPython 3.12.15:

```sh
python3 -I -B research/p112-tetrad-dual-anchor-screen/verify.py
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/p112-tetrad-dual-anchor-screen --check-only
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/p112-tetrad-dual-anchor-screen
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/p112-tetrad-cut-consumer --check-only
python3.12 research/p112-tetrad-cut-consumer/verify.py
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/p112-tetrad-cut-consumer
```

The checks cover all 14 blocks, 56 copy ranks, exact basis and cut identities, the dirty-state counterexample and correction, mutation controls, and the four-prefix sensitivity cases. No full selected cold replay, physical supplier, dirty-input retention channel, complete outer invoice, or proof-kernel review is claimed.

## Credit

Exact source pins are in each package's `SOURCES.json`. The P112 geometry, selected-port bijection, gauge44 word and bit-side pricing retain predecessor attribution. This follow-up adds the unimodular-kernel witness, transformed cut map and dirty-baseline audit. Prepared by Gonzalo Mier with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; Apache-2.0. No independent human or proof-kernel review is claimed.

## Open next questions

1. Can a source-bound native schedule provide `Jx` at the pre-B consumer while preserving the selected dirty state and endpoint?
2. What is the actual scalar tariff, including adapters, lifetime and restoration, for the changed coefficients?
3. Can a complete source-bound supplier and admitted bit-side invoice keep the joint target above `0.003`?
